Finishing an ironman is impressive, but at 15 hours, 19 minutes he didn't win anything - not even his age group.

You're right. He didn't win. He completed it.

Traditionally, just completing the triathlon is considered it's own reward. All who complete it are called "Ironmen".

IIRC, there was a case where a female tri-athelete fell down due to exhaustion, but crawled the rest of the race just to complete it. That's the appeal of the Ironman triathlon.

Yes, that was Julie Moss... waaaaaay back in the day. She was racing to win, not just to finish. She didn't win. Crawling would be considered really poor form nowadays.

I've completed an ironman, and yes I am an ironman, but the people who race ironman to win are beasts of an entirely different breed. I have respect for my fellow ironmen/women; I have reverence and awe for people who finish 140.6 in just a little over 8 hours.

Wow! An ironman among us!

If you don't mind sharing, when did you complete the triathlon? Do you plan on redoing it?

Also, thanks for correcting me about Julie Moss.

I did the ironman in 2007. In 1996 I finished my first marathon and decided that I wanted to do triathlons, and ironman was a dream that took me a little over ten years to realize. I was very inspired by those early ironman broadcasts, and the stories of the triathletes in the old days; Dave Scott was my idol.

Finishing was an incredible moment, and I even enjoyed all of the training that lead up to it because it was my life's passion at the time, but no, I have no plans to do another. Training consumed every weekend and most mornings and evenings for almost a year, and for someone with a family it can be something of a selfish sport. With entry fees, nutrition, bike parts/repairs, etc., it's a bit expensive, too. It was worth it, though. :)
